context:
Goal: reviewed lane PRs reach main with the least CI and the least waiting.
Problem (goal): the consultant reports that since 21:45 CST Nov 13, 9 combine PRs opened and 0 merged (4 closed, 5 open), while all 7 claude-settings merges were single PRs. Degen merged 10 single PRs per lane between 00:36 and 01:43 CST. Triage's REST read of the 30 most recently closed claude-settings PRs (partial, to 04:06 UTC): 6 combine PRs closed unmerged (#3360, #3361, #3363, #3314, #3315, #3356), none merged; 6 single PRs merged (#3345, #3342, #3149, #3317, #3323, #3269). The 4-closed and 5-open split is not reproduced (6 closed on that page); the total of 9 is not checked.
Based on (ruling): your words 21:45 CST (own-combine-tournament-idea: combine merge queues pairwise on dry trees while a run is in CI) and 21:48 CST (own-rolling-combine-train: combining continuous, the runner a scaling machine) and 767 a (a PR merges alone; it may combine several reviewed lanes when that saves CI). Based on (measured, consultant, relayed): the counts above, partly read by triage.
Safety note for Degen (consultant, relayed, unchecked): 5 PRs merged within 60 s at 01:42 to 01:43 CST onto a main whose push runs had not finished, so a red run cannot be blamed on one PR; #687 merged 28 s after #677 while #677's main run (later red: server shard 2 test) was running; the next run was green; cause unread.
Departs from: main — your two ideas make combining the standing duty; a pauses the tournament and the train, adds fast dry checks before each PR goes ready, and keeps combining only for a real conflict; b builds the tournament as designed, automated, with a review after 3 batches; c changes nothing.
Added 02:13 CST (consultant, from runner 10's 02:12 answer, relayed; unchecked by triage): the tournament was not run as designed. It ran one dry fold, by hand, once; there were no continuous folds; the fast checks per round did not run, so each combine's first check was the 24 to 27 min lane lint. Of the four failed combines, three (#3361 split guard, #3363 STE lint, #3360 open-PR clash) would have dropped in seconds on a dry-tree fast check; #3314 and #3315 closed as replaced. Per-batch numbers were never posted. Reframed 02:14 CST (consultant, relayed): main already merges per lane (decision all-repos-switch-together, your 09:42 CST Nov 12 word; R42), so the only open question is whether to keep your later combine-train ruling (own-rolling-combine-train, 21:48 CST Nov 13, filed here; the consultant wrote 21:45, which is the tournament idea's time), which is not on main yet. The consultant dropped the earlier option "keep as is"; the two options below are its reframe. Departs from: main — per-lane merge — adds the combine train (b); a leaves main as it is, plus the quick checks.
Meanwhile: runners keep merging by priority under own-ready-by-priority; no lane is told to stop or start combining until you answer.
home: rulings own-combine-tournament-idea (21:45 CST Nov 13), own-rolling-combine-train (21:48 CST Nov 13), own-767-a-combined-pr; steps combine-tournament, batch-runner-rolling-train
lastAnswer: 826: typed in chat 02:14 CST, relayed by the consultant: "can’t we do a while work on building b" (read as: do a now while building b).

options.gain: No new machinery; the cheap checks that would have dropped three of the four failed combines in seconds run on every PR; merges keep the path that landed everything since 21:45 CST.
options.label: Withdraw the train ruling: stay per-lane as main is, plus the quick dry checks (STE lint, split guard, cost pins, scaffold, debt retire, open-PR clash) before each ready mark; combine only for a real conflict (recommended by the consultant)
options.lose: Your continuous-train idea (21:48 CST) and the tournament idea (21:45 CST) rest unbuilt; the combine saving stays unmeasured.

options.gain: Your idea gets a fair test; per-batch numbers get posted.
options.label: Keep the train ruling: build the tournament and train as designed, automated, with fast checks every fold round; review after 3 batches
options.lose: The automation and fast-check rounds come first; combine PRs may still not merge; a combine step is added on top of per-lane merging.

owner: consultant (session_013NEJKz5AWFJhGvmCUoi6wQ), 01:55 CST Nov 14; posted by triage (session_013NEJKzCzoWhfP8FMCPtQU6)
reply: Your word, as the consultant relayed it (it did not land on this page, so triage read it from the relay): "can’t we do a while work on building b". Read as: merge per lane by priority now, with the quick dry checks before each ready mark (a); meanwhile build the combine train as designed and automated (b): continuous dry folds, fast checks every round, per-batch numbers, review after 3 batches; switch to the train only once it runs and its numbers beat per-lane. Filed as ruling own-826-a-now-build-b. The wording is open to another reading; if that is not what you meant, say so and triage reopens this. Two steps for the build: fast-checks-before-ready (now) and combine-train-tool (tracker: the coordinator, path ALONE, its own PR). No lane stops or starts combining by hand meanwhile.
short: Keep the combine train ruling, or stay per-lane with quick checks before ready?
title: Main already merges per lane (your 09:42 CST Nov 12 word, decision all-repos-switch-together). The open question is only whether to keep your 21:48 CST Nov 13 ruling that adds a continuous combine train on top. Withdraw it and stay per-lane, with quick dry checks before each ready mark (a), or keep it, built as designed and automated (b)?
why: Both the tournament (21:45 CST Nov 13) and the rolling train (21:48 CST Nov 13) are your ideas, so pausing one is yours to say. The consultant measured the stale result; triage read part of it by REST.
